title: Crafts Museum, Delhi | History, Timings & Travel Guide
content:
Crafts Museum - Delhi,

The Crafts Museum in Delhi is one of the most unique places in the capital. Located near Pragati Maidan, it is a living showcase of India’s traditional arts and crafts. Established in 1956, this museum was designed to preserve and celebrate India’s rich craft heritage at a time when modernization was rapidly changing lifestyles.

Spread over a large area, the museum houses over 35,000 rare and precious objects — including wood carvings, tribal paintings, handmade textiles, metal crafts, and clay art. But what makes the Crafts Museum even more special is its atmosphere. With mud huts, village courtyards, and craftsmen at work, it feels like you are visiting a traditional Indian village right in the heart of Delhi.

Walking through the galleries, you can see:

  • Textile treasures like rare Kashmiri shawls, Banarasi saris, and tribal weaves.
  • Folk paintings such as Madhubani, Pattachitra, and Warli art.
  • Terracotta figures and clay sculptures from different states of India.
  • Everyday household objects that tell stories of rural life.

Outside, in the village complex, artisans from across the country often demonstrate weaving, pottery, painting, and embroidery. You can even buy authentic handicrafts directly from them-making your visit both cultural and memorable.

The museum also has a cafe called Cafe Lota, which is loved for its fusion of traditional Indian flavors and modern twists. It’s a favorite spot for both locals and travelers.

Visitor Information:

  • Location: Pragati Maidan, Bhairon Marg, New Delhi.
  • Timings: 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM (Closed on Mondays and public holidays).
  • Entry Fee: ₹20 for Indian visitors, ₹200 for foreigners. Free for children below 12 years.
  • Best Time to Visit: The museum is open throughout the year, but October to March is most comfortable for exploring Delhi.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: The nearest metro station is Pragati Maidan (Blue Line), just a short walk away.
  • By Bus/Auto: Well-connected by DTC buses and auto-rickshaws from all parts of Delhi.
  • By Car: Easily accessible by road.

Parking Information: Paid parking is available near Pragati Maidan, but it may get crowded during exhibitions and fairs.

Nearby Places to Visit:

  • India Gate - Iconic war memorial, perfect for evening strolls.
  • National Science Centre - Great for kids and families.
  • Purana Qila (Old Fort) - A historic fort located just next to the museum.
  • National Zoological Park (Delhi Zoo) – Popular family attraction nearby.

Travel Tip: If you love shopping, try visiting during craft fairs or festivals when the museum hosts artisans from all over India - it’s the best time to see live art and grab unique souvenirs.
excerpt: The Crafts Museum in Delhi, also known as the National Handicrafts and Handlooms Museum, is a beautiful place that brings India’s traditional arts alive. With its wide collection of textiles, paintings, carvings, and village-style settings, it feels like stepping into a living heritage. It’s not just a museum - it’s an experience of India’s culture, crafts, and creativity
